commit.message:
Add get-screenshot app tool to the map-server example (#821)

The map view already captures scaled PNG screenshots of the globe for
model-context updates, but only pushed them opportunistically (and only
when the host supports images in updateModelContext). This factors that
capture into a shared helper and registers a get-screenshot view tool,
so the model can request the current view on demand and see exactly
what the user sees. Takes an optional maxDimension (default 1024px) to
trade detail against image token cost.

The e2e test follows the pdf-get-current-pdf pattern: it plays the
host, posting tools/list and tools/call JSON-RPC into the app iframe
from the sandbox frame.

Co-authored-by: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
Update dependencies to clear npm audit findings (#793)

Bump solid-js in basic-server-solid from the exact 1.9.10 to 1.9.15. 1.9.10 depends on seroval ~1.3, which has open advisories (fixed in 1.5.3), so anyone installing the published @modelcontextprotocol/server-basic-solid gets it. The root overrides that pinned seroval 1.4.1 and seroval-plugins 1.4.2 are removed because solid-js 1.9.15 needs seroval ~1.5.4, and the solid-js override moves to 1.9.15.

The lockfile is refreshed with npm audit fix (patch and minor updates only), which clears the remaining findings in hono, qs, undici, postcss, nanoid, devalue, sharp, brace-expansion and fflate. npm audit now reports 0 vulnerabilities.

commit.message:
Pin @cantoo/pdf-lib to 2.6.5 in pdf-server (#792)

The ^2.6.5 range lets a fresh install of @modelcontextprotocol/server-pdf resolve @cantoo/pdf-lib 2.11.x, which the lockfile and CI never test. 2.11.0 also added new dependencies with open-ended ranges (culori >=4, node-html-better-parser), and the supply-chain checks on 2.11.0 and culori 4.0.2 report findings. The lockfile and CI already use 2.6.5, whose dependency tree passes those checks, so pin exactly that version.

commit.message:
Bump version to 2.0.2

Patch release that ships the exact pdfjs-dist pin for @modelcontextprotocol/server-pdf (#789), so fresh installs no longer resolve a pdfjs-dist version affected by GHSA-hq66-cqwq-w95j.

Pin pdfjs-dist to 5.4.530 in pdf-server

The ^5.0.0 range lets a fresh install of @modelcontextprotocol/server-pdf resolve pdfjs-dist 5.7.x, which is affected by GHSA-hq66-cqwq-w95j (arbitrary JavaScript execution when opening a crafted PDF; fixed only in 6.2.108). The lockfile and CI already use 5.4.530, which is outside the affected range (5.6.83 to 6.2.108), so pin exactly that version.

Fix dependency isolation check against @modelcontextprotocol/client 2.1

client 2.1.0 typings reference ErrorOptions, which needs the ES2022.Error lib. The check compiles its throwaway consumers with lib ES2020 and skipLibCheck off, so it failed once npm resolved the auto-installed client peer to 2.1.0.

Bump version to 2.0.1

Patch release picking up the fix for example servers crashing at startup on Node older than 20.11 (#787) and the canonical repository.url form (#773).

Fix example servers crashing at startup on Node older than 20.11

The example servers located their dist directory with
import.meta.filename / import.meta.dirname, which only exist from
Node 20.11. On older versions (18.x, 20.0 to 20.10) the module threw
"TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'endsWith')"
at load, before the server could answer `initialize`, even though the
packages are documented as supporting Node 20+.

- Derive the path from import.meta.url with fileURLToPath, the idiom
  lazy-auth-server already uses, in the 21 affected example servers and
  in the quickstart (docs/quickstart.md resynced).
- Declare engines.node ">=20" in the published example packages and
  record it in package-lock.json.
- CI: after the MCPB smoke test, run the same pdf-server bundle on
  Node 20.0.0 so a regression fails the build.

commit.message:
Use the canonical git+https form for repository.url

npm normalizes the bare https URL to git+https://….git at publish time
and warns about it on every package. Storing the canonical form removes
the warning and matches what npm's trusted-publisher check compares
against the repository.

commit.message:
CI: build the WSL job on ext4, skip the unused Chromium download, list tsconfig types

The Windows WSL job is the critical path of every CI run (589 to 752 s).
Its checkout sits on the Windows drive, which WSL reaches over 9P, and
writing node_modules there is what makes npm ci take about three minutes
where the Linux job takes 23 s. The step now copies the tree onto the
distro's ext4 filesystem before installing and building, as Microsoft's
WSL guidance recommends for I/O-heavy work.

The e2e job downloaded the full Chromium build (about 165 MB) on every
run, but a headless run with no channel launches chromium-headless-shell
and never opens it. `--only-shell` skips that download.

Every tsconfig now lists the @types packages it uses (node, bun,
vite/client, dom-speech-recognition) instead of relying on TypeScript
auto-including everything under node_modules/@types. On TypeScript 5.9
this is a no-op: identical diagnostics across all 48 projects and
byte-identical emitted .d.ts files. It is a prerequisite for TypeScript 7,
which drops the auto-inclusion; with these lists the Go compiler passes
all 48 projects, so that upgrade becomes a version bump once TypeDoc
supports it.

Two cache-based approaches were evaluated and rejected: an npm cache for
the WSL job (npm ci is slow there because of 9P, not downloads, and a
prefix-restored cache grows without bound) and a Playwright browser cache
(Playwright's docs advise against it; the download is under 10 s).

Migration guide fixes and editor-visible deprecation for the 1.x handler form (#771)

Guide fact-checked claim by claim against the built package: three wording fixes, seven coverage gaps (including the double-registration guard now covering the base Protocol's progress/cancelled handlers), and the legacy setRequestHandler overload's @deprecated moved onto a documented call signature so editors report it.
